title: Node input manifest
description: The exact, enumerated set of bytes a node receives. A node never inherits context; it receives this. Isolation is a property of the runner, and this file is the shape of that property — which is what makes it testable rather than hoped for.

cwd.description: Where the node runs. Measured, not assumed: auto-memory is keyed by project path, so a node launched inside the project directory receives the operator's memory index — Builder-authored free text arriving in the Reviewer's context. Running in the node's own worktree is what closes that channel. See tests/test_manifest.py::MemoryChannel.

inputs.description: Only the keys this node type declares in node-types.json. Anything else is stripped at assembly rather than forwarded — an undeclared field is exactly how a Builder would argue its case to a Reviewer.

file.description: A referenced file: where it is, and the hash of what it said. The path alone would let content change under a recorded manifest, which would make the manifest hash evidence of nothing.

criteria.description: The acceptance criteria, as a list. The Reviewer judges against these and its approval must name which it checked — so they arrive as discrete items rather than a paragraph to interpret.

diff.description: A sha range, not a blob. The node reads the diff with the tools its policy grants; naming the range is what bounds WHAT it may look at, while the tool policy bounds HOW.

findings.description: Reviewer findings travelling to Repair. The one place prose crosses between nodes, and it crosses in the direction that cannot buy an approval.
